description:
FILED s540a (Opus agent, 2026-11-13) from the CPAN board timing (#4787; docs/cpan-speed-comparison-s540.md section 4, the per-file table baselines/board-timing-s540.tsv; tool tools/board-timing.pl).  Times are CPU seconds, code 381d9063 (MAIN-READY-89), coarse pass load-normalised, lever A/Bs on a quiet box (heavy.sh bench, best of 3).

WHAT: mcompile -- SBCL's native compile of a cached module TEXT -- is 1,422.5 s of PCL's 2,169 s over the 638 compared board files (612 files, 28 dists): Pod::Simple 7.3 s per test file, Text::CSV_PP 4.6 s, Template Toolkit 3.4 s, Getopt::Long 3.1 s, Data::Dumper 1.5 s.  The cause is the compile POLICY, not a bug: %p-compile-module-p answers "fasl" only for perl's installed library dirs + PCL's own lib/ (DECIDED s471: PCL_COMPILE_DIRS default; "a module that is not compiled still gets the .lisp cache and the manifest check ... correctness is the manifest, this is a belt"), so the module under development -- in a test suite: the module under test -- is recompiled by SBCL from its cached text in every file.

EVIDENCE: load-phase profiles (tools/board-timing.pl --prof cpu --prof-from start, 6 files of 6 dists, on 05806e16): SBCL's compiler -- find-and-propagate-constraints 30-33 %, ir1-optimize 26-30 %, ir1-convert 10-13 %.

DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (TAKEN, scratch/s540a/bench2b.log + bench2-L2-*.tsv): PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*' vs the default, best of 3: Text-CSV 16_import.t 5.29 -> 0.68 s; Getopt-Long gol-load1.t 3.82 -> 0.58; JSON-PP 000_load.t 1.82 -> 0.37; Data-Dumper bless.t 2.49 -> 0.64; HTTP-Tiny 140_proxy.t 2.70 -> 1.36; TT config.t 4.59 -> 2.31 and Log4perl 040Filter.t 4.63 -> 4.38 still converging at run 3 (#4963).  CAUTION for whoever measures again: PCL_COMPILE_DIRS=<one dir> REPLACES the default list (perl's installed modules then load from text -- Algorithm-Diff oo.t 1.54 -> 3.18 s); use '*' or list the defaults too.  The alternative measured and REJECTED as the main lever: a cheap compile policy for every run-time compile (proclaim compilation-speed 3, speed 0) -- only -0..-25 % (Getopt 3.82 -> 3.17, JSON-PP 1.82 -> 1.44).

THE QUESTION FOR THE RULING: may a module under -I / lib / PERL5LIB get a fasl (validated exactly as the installed ones are), by default -- or behind a switch the board and test runners set?  The s471 reason was opacity, not staleness (the manifest already decides validity).  Size once ruled: one session (the default list in %p-compile-module-p + the guards that assert it, Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t et al.).
subject: PERF (CPAN board #1, 1,422 s of 2,169): the distribution's own modules (any module under -I / lib / PERL5LIB) are compiled from TEXT by SBCL on EVERY run -- %p-compile-module-p fasl-caches only perl's installed dirs + PCL's lib/ (the s471 ruling); PCL_COMPILE_DIRS='*' takes a board file from 5.29 s to 0.68 s -- NEEDS A RULING
